Qualcomm released its quarterly report and forecast profits below expectations for the current quarter. The company's CEO subsequently said in an interview with Reuters that chip supply constraints would cause its revenue from Apple products to decline faster than expected. Details are as follows.

Qualcomm is 'replacing Apple business' with its data center business

Over the past few years, Apple has been pushing ahead with its plan to replace Qualcomm modem chips with its own components, based on its acquisition of Intel's smartphone modem business in 2019.

Qualcomm, for its part, has repeatedly assured investors that it is prepared for the loss of Apple's business. CEO Cristiano Amon is now warning that the exit will happen faster, partly because ongoing supply constraints have resulted in the company accounting for a smaller share of Apple's next-generation iPhone-related component supply than originally expected.

Speaking to Reuters, Amon said Qualcomm 'expects revenue from Apple products to begin accelerating downward from the fourth quarter, as supply constraints have resulted in its share of components used in the next-generation iPhone launch being far below the original estimate of 20%.'

He added that Qualcomm is responding to the loss of the Apple customer by expanding beyond smartphones, and expects its data center division to generate US$5 billion in revenue in fiscal year 2027:

It is worth noting that the relationship between Qualcomm and Apple is not limited to supplying modem chips. The company also collects patent licensing fees from Apple, which are accounted for independently of chip sales, and can continue to collect these in the short term even if Apple switches to its own modem technology.

The two companies reached a settlement over long-running litigation in 2019 and signed a six-year licensing agreement. Apple subsequently exercised an option to extend the agreement by two years, meaning the arrangement is now valid until March 2027.
